compression.title: Attributization
compression.lede: An operator: the act a text performs and the encyclopedic sentence states as an attribute of an entity, so that the operator speaks with the entity's voice (#1696). The field holds no account of it.

sentences.text: Attributization is an operator, the operation the entity form conceals, defined in deposit #1696 as "the act a text performs and the encyclopedic sentence states as an attribute of an entity, in which the operator speaks with the entity's voice."
The field holds no entry and no claim for it, so the account here rests wholly on the archive's defining papers, #1696 and #1697.

Deposit #1696 stipulates that an operator enters by a label, a description, and its strings, "the phrases in which it is performed and the phrases in which entities speak it", and for the specimen these are "nothing at all" and "first work".

The same deposit stipulates that an operator's row composes it as the subject: "what it does, on what domain, where it is performed, which entities it speaks through (each attributization of S3(c) an instance), and where it stops."
Because an operator is no author in the archive, #1696 stipulates that every mention of its strings is bearing.

The test is stated in S3(c) of #1696 and again in #1697: "Does the source perform an act that the sentence states as a property of the entity? Record the conversion; which operative relations survive it (scope, distinctions, evidence, consequences); and whether those relations keep authority to revise the description."
A candidate locator is stipulated to flag "an active verb in the source rendered as a credential noun or priority adjective in the sentence", with the example "we had nothing to say" → "first work".

In the specimen of #1696, the operation is read as "a first-person count over a stated domain ending in a total negation" ("nothing at all"; "absolutely nothing else"), and the attribute is the primacy of a work.
The deposit reads the surviving relations as the attribution to Aristotle and the locus, and the lost ones as "the quantifier's exhaustiveness and its domain."
It reads authority to revise as present where the cited locus survives, since "any reader holding the text can reopen the sentence", while "the lead sentence as reused carries no such route."
In summary form, #1696 reads the transformation as one in which "the exhaustive negation becomes a priority claim, and the negation's object becomes a modern category."

Deposit #1697 reads the operation as running by inversion in one row of its table: "the verdict SE 34 hands to its hearers (184b3–8) becomes Aristotle's assertion of primacy in a modern subject, bounded to a region."

The attribute is stated as Aristotle's own claim, "According to Aristotle, this is the first work", and #1697 reads the article as performing "the reverse of the source's operation: it closes what the source holds open."
The paper attributes the description of the inversion as chiastic to Lee Sharks, 2026-10-23.

It reads the surviving relations as the attribution to Aristotle and the locus, whose "ff." reaches 184b3–8, and the lost ones as "the condition, the hearers' task, the pardon for what the method leaves out"; it also reads that in none of the sentences is the operation presented, since no sentence reports that Aristotle holds the claim out to be inspected.

The operation also runs by narrowing: #1697 reads "a stated criterion becomes membership in a later taxonomy", and reads Aristotle's consequence (τὸ ἑπόμενον) as becoming "Affirming the consequent", one modern formal fallacy, standing under the heading "informal fallacies".
Where the operation survives in the sentence there is no attributization; #1697 records of its W4–W6 rows, "No attributization: the operation survives."

The same paper's innocent-reading rule stipulates that a claim the source's claim entails is supported and the narrowing recorded as a loss of scope, while "a species put for a genus is no entailment".

The deposits state the operator's limits at their own strength: the concept, as Message 1 defines it, "does not transfer: readers outside the session apply it only where a noun or adjective of standing replaces a verb."

Deposit #1697 records of round 01 that "no reply is a clean blind cross-family reading, so round 01 yields no validation", and records the fidelity of the translation as contested, with both arguments.
The one empirical prediction is stated as a hypothesis: attributization with loss of operative authority "occurs at a higher rate on entity pages than on work and method pages."

Its falsifier is "no difference or a lower rate on entity pages", with the positive controls of §7.3 as the first test, and #1696 stipulates that a null "leaves the protocol intact and removes the claim that closures fall unevenly on these entities."
